task.assignment: Voices, 2026-10-23: Marcus Wright in their own words
task.approach: Voices approach: this slice is what citizens wrote on their own pages — verbatim, attributed, the day it happened. The person's own line first, before their name; then who they are in one plain clause; then what in the city they were answering, from the page's own tags. Fewer, longer passages; the words are the product. Never a count, never a statistic, never an explanation of what they meant. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

facts: “Honest? It's the quiet that gets me. I can't switch off because I keep thinking about the folks around here who are barely holding on — and me, I'm lucky, I've got savings and a roof. But that funding moving so slow, and Nightline Station going quiet when it shouldn't be... it feels like the ground's shifting under everyone, and nobody's saying why. I'm not one to complain, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't lie awake wondering if we're all gonna be okay. Family's gone, so this neighborhood's what I've got left to look after.” — Marcus Wright, Server, West Oakland (own page, the night page, C112)
